papers.title_en: Spectrally smooth broadband response via autocorrelation-constrained inverse design
papers.authors: Johannes Gedeon, Rasmus E. Christiansen, Ole Sigmund
papers.evidence: 基于自相关约束的逆向设计实现光谱平滑宽带响应，可用于AR波导光栅优化
papers.tldr: 时间域逆设计通常采用时间积分场量作为目标，虽能最大化宽带总响应，却无法抑制带内纹波、窄特征或旁瓣。本文提出一种基于加权长滞后自相关能量的时域度量，将其作为自相关约束引入目标函数，以量化并惩罚光谱变化。该方法嵌入FDTD拓扑优化框架，在一维介质布拉格镜逆设计中验证，有效获得光谱平滑的宽带响应。
papers.abstract_en: Time-domain inverse design in photonics is known to be suitable for maximizing the efficiency of optical devices over broad frequency ranges. Objectives commonly used in this context include time-integrated field quantities derived from Poynting's theorem, such as energy, flux, or dissipated power, which can be directly linked to integrated frequency-domain responses via Parseval's theorem. While computationally efficient, these objectives measure only the total response over the targeted bandwidth and, as we demonstrate, are insufficient to capture undesired in-band ripple, narrow spectral features, or sidelobes. We overcome this limitation by introducing a time-domain metric quantifying such spectral variations based on the weighted long-lag autocorrelation energy of the optical response. We incorporate this metric into an FDTD-based topology-optimization framework and demonstrate its beneficial effect on the example of inverse designing one-dimensional dielectric Bragg mirrors via the time-domain adjoint method.

papers.title_en: Spectrally smooth broadband response via autocorrelation-constrained inverse design
papers.authors: Johannes Gedeon, Rasmus Ellebæk Christiansen, Ole Sigmund
papers.evidence: 基于自相关约束的逆向设计实现光谱平滑宽带响应，可用于AR波导光栅优化
papers.tldr: 时域逆设计在宽频光子器件优化中具有计算优势，但常用目标函数仅度量总响应，无法捕捉带内波纹、窄谱特征和旁瓣等光谱缺陷。针对这一问题，本文提出一种基于加权长滞后自相关能量的时域度量，用于量化光谱变化，并将其集成到基于 FDTD 的拓扑优化框架中。在一维介电布拉格镜的逆设计实例中，该方法成功抑制了不期望的光谱起伏，实现了平滑的宽带响应。该工作扩展了时域逆设计对光谱细节的控制能力，为高性能宽带光子器件设计提供了新途径。

We overcome this limitation by introducing a time-domain metric quantifying such spectral variations based on the weighted long-lag autocorrelation energy of the optical response.
